[project]
name = "jobspy-mcp"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "MCP server wrapping JobSpy for the Jobs for AI Agents plugin"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = [
    "mcp>=1.1.0",
    "python-jobspy>=1.1.82",
    "pandas>=2.1.0",
]

[project.scripts]
jobspy-mcp = "job_server:mcp.run"

"""
Smoke tests for the JobSpy MCP server.

Verifies that the server imports cleanly, tools are registered,
and helper functions work correctly. Does NOT make real network
calls to job boards — that requires manual integration testing.
"""

import json
from datetime import date, datetime

# Test date serializer
from job_server import _serialize_dates, _format_job_results, VALID_SITES, VALID_JOB_TYPES
import pandas as pd


def test_serialize_dates():
    assert _serialize_dates(date(2026, 3, 31)) == "2026-03-31"
    assert _serialize_dates(datetime(2026, 3, 31, 12, 0)) == "2026-03-31T12:00:00"
    try:
        _serialize_dates("not a date")
        assert False, "Should have raised TypeError"
    except TypeError:
        pass


def test_format_job_results_empty():
    df = pd.DataFrame()
    result = _format_job_results(df)
    parsed = json.loads(result)
    assert parsed == []


def test_format_job_results_with_data():
    df = pd.DataFrame([{
        "title": "Software Engineer",
        "company": "Acme Corp",
        "location": "San Francisco, CA",
        "date_posted": date(2026, 3, 30),
        "job_url": "https://example.com/job/123",
        "job_type": "fulltime",
        "is_remote": False,
        "min_amount": 120000,
        "max_amount": 180000,
        "currency": "USD",
        "interval": "yearly",
        "site": "indeed",
        "description": "Build great software.",
    }])
    result = _format_job_results(df)
    parsed = json.loads(result)
    assert len(parsed) == 1
    assert parsed[0]["title"] == "Software Engineer"
    assert parsed[0]["company"] == "Acme Corp"
    assert parsed[0]["min_amount"] == 120000


def test_format_job_results_handles_nan():
    df = pd.DataFrame([{
        "title": "Designer",
        "company": "StartupXYZ",
        "location": "Remote",
        "min_amount": float("nan"),
        "max_amount": float("nan"),
    }])
    result = _format_job_results(df)
    parsed = json.loads(result)
    assert parsed[0]["min_amount"] is None
    assert parsed[0]["max_amount"] is None


def test_valid_sites_list():
    assert "indeed" in VALID_SITES
    assert "linkedin" in VALID_SITES
    assert "glassdoor" in VALID_SITES
    assert "zip_recruiter" in VALID_SITES
    assert "google" in VALID_SITES
    assert "bayt" in VALID_SITES
    assert "naukri" in VALID_SITES
    assert "bdjobs" in VALID_SITES
    assert len(VALID_SITES) == 8


def test_valid_job_types():
    assert VALID_JOB_TYPES == ["fulltime", "parttime", "internship", "contract"]


def test_get_supported_sites():
    from job_server import get_supported_sites
    result = get_supported_sites()
    assert "## Supported Job Boards" in result
    for site in VALID_SITES:
        assert site in result


def test_get_search_tips():
    from job_server import get_search_tips
    result = get_search_tips()
    assert "## Job Search Tips" in result
    assert "Search terms" in result


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_serialize_dates()
    test_format_job_results_empty()
    test_format_job_results_with_data()
    test_format_job_results_handles_nan()
    test_valid_sites_list()
    test_valid_job_types()
    test_get_supported_sites()
    test_get_search_tips()
    print("All tests passed!")

"""
JobSpy MCP Server for Jobs for AI Agents plugin.

Thin wrapper around python-jobspy. Exposes job scraping as MCP tools.
All intelligence (resume handling, company research, etc.) lives in
skills and agents — this server just scrapes.

Based on: https://github.com/lowcoordination/mcp-jobspy
Additional tools from: https://github.com/chinpeerapat/jobspy-mcp-server
"""

import json
import logging
from datetime import date, datetime
from typing import Optional

import pandas as pd
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
from jobspy import scrape_jobs

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger("jobspy-mcp")

mcp = FastMCP("JobSpy Job Search")

VALID_SITES = [
    "indeed", "linkedin", "glassdoor", "zip_recruiter",
    "google", "bayt", "naukri", "bdjobs",
]

VALID_JOB_TYPES = ["fulltime", "parttime", "internship", "contract"]

DEFAULT_SITES = ["indeed", "linkedin", "zip_recruiter", "google"]
DEFAULT_RESULTS = 15
DEFAULT_HOURS_OLD = 72
DEFAULT_DISTANCE = 50
DEFAULT_COUNTRY = "usa"


def _serialize_dates(obj):
    """JSON serializer for date/datetime objects."""
    if isinstance(obj, (date, datetime)):
        return obj.isoformat()
    raise TypeError(f"Type {type(obj)} not serializable")


def _format_job_results(df: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
    """Format a DataFrame of jobs into readable JSON for Claude."""
    cols = [
        "title", "company", "location", "date_posted", "job_url",
        "job_type", "is_remote", "min_amount", "max_amount",
        "currency", "interval", "site", "description",
    ]
    available_cols = [c for c in cols if c in df.columns]
    records = df[available_cols].to_dict(orient="records")

    # Clean NaN values — JSON doesn't support them
    for record in records:
        for key, value in record.items():
            if pd.isna(value):
                record[key] = None

    return json.dumps(records, indent=2, default=_serialize_dates)


@mcp.tool()
def search_jobs(
    search_term: str,
    location: str = "USA",
    site_name: Optional[list[str]] = None,
    results_wanted: int = DEFAULT_RESULTS,
    hours_old: int = DEFAULT_HOURS_OLD,
    job_type: Optional[str] = None,
    is_remote: bool = False,
    distance: int = DEFAULT_DISTANCE,
    country: str = DEFAULT_COUNTRY,
    description_format: str = "markdown",
) -> str:
    """
    Search for jobs across multiple job boards.

    Args:
        search_term: Job search keywords (e.g., 'software engineer', 'data scientist')
        location: Job location (e.g., 'San Francisco, CA', 'Remote')
        site_name: Job boards to search. Options: indeed, linkedin, glassdoor,
                   zip_recruiter, google, bayt, naukri, bdjobs.
                   Defaults to indeed, linkedin, zip_recruiter, google.
        results_wanted: Number of results to retrieve (1-100)
        hours_old: Only show jobs posted within this many hours
        job_type: Filter by type: fulltime, parttime, internship, contract
        is_remote: Set to true for remote-only jobs
        distance: Search radius in miles from location
        country: Country for Indeed/Glassdoor (e.g., 'usa', 'uk', 'canada')
        description_format: Format for descriptions: 'markdown' or 'html'

    Returns:
        JSON array of job objects with title, company, location, salary,
        url, description, and more.
    """
    sites = site_name if site_name else DEFAULT_SITES

    invalid = [s for s in sites if s not in VALID_SITES]
    if invalid:
        return json.dumps({
            "error": f"Invalid site(s): {invalid}. Valid: {VALID_SITES}"
        })

    if job_type and job_type not in VALID_JOB_TYPES:
        return json.dumps({
            "error": f"Invalid job_type: {job_type}. Valid: {VALID_JOB_TYPES}"
        })

    try:
        logger.info(f"Searching for '{search_term}' in '{location}' on {sites}")

        df = scrape_jobs(
            site_name=sites,
            search_term=search_term,
            location=location,
            results_wanted=results_wanted,
            hours_old=hours_old,
            job_type=job_type,
            is_remote=is_remote,
            distance=distance,
            country_indeed=country,
            description_format=description_format,
        )

        if df.empty:
            return json.dumps({"results": [], "message": "No jobs found. Try broader search terms or different sites."})

        logger.info(f"Found {len(df)} jobs")
        return _format_job_results(df)

    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Search failed: {e}")
        return json.dumps({"error": str(e)})


@mcp.tool()
def get_supported_sites() -> str:
    """
    Get list of supported job boards with descriptions.

    Returns:
        Formatted list of all 8 supported job boards.
    """
    sites = {
        "indeed": "Indeed — largest global job search engine, most reliable, least rate limiting",
        "linkedin": "LinkedIn — professional networking, quality listings but strict rate limits",
        "glassdoor": "Glassdoor — job listings with company reviews and salary data",
        "zip_recruiter": "ZipRecruiter — job matching platform, US/Canada focus",
        "google": "Google Jobs — aggregated listings from across the web",
        "bayt": "Bayt — Middle East focused job portal",
        "naukri": "Naukri — India's leading job portal, includes skills and experience data",
        "bdjobs": "BDJobs — Bangladesh's premier job portal",
    }

    lines = [f"- **{name}**: {desc}" for name, desc in sites.items()]
    return "## Supported Job Boards\n\n" + "\n".join(lines)


@mcp.tool()
def get_supported_countries() -> str:
    """
    Get list of supported countries for job searches.

    Returns:
        List of supported countries for the country parameter.
    """
    try:
        from jobspy.model import Country
        countries = []
        for c in Country:
            names = c.value[0] if isinstance(c.value, tuple) else c.value
            countries.append(f"- **{c.name}**: {names}")
        return "## Supported Countries\n\n" + "\n".join(sorted(countries))
    except ImportError:
        return (
            "## Common Countries\n\n"
            "usa, uk, canada, australia, germany, france, india, singapore, "
            "brazil, mexico, japan, south korea, netherlands, sweden, ireland"
        )


@mcp.tool()
def get_search_tips() -> str:
    """
    Get tips for effective job searching.

    Returns:
        Best practices for getting good search results.
    """
    return """## Job Search Tips

**Search terms:**
- Be specific: "Python developer" beats "developer"
- Try variations: "software engineer", "software developer", "SWE"
- Include level: "senior", "junior", "lead", "staff"
- Include tech: "React developer", "AWS engineer"

**Site selection:**
- Start with indeed + zip_recruiter (most reliable)
- Add linkedin for quality but expect rate limits
- Use regional sites for specific markets (bayt, naukri, bdjobs)

**Filters:**
- Use hours_old=24 for fresh postings
- Start with 10-15 results, increase if needed
- Set is_remote=true for remote-only jobs
- Adjust distance for local vs. wide searches

**If no results:** Broaden search terms, try different sites, increase hours_old, or try a different location."""


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()

# Jobs for AI Agents ### Your AI job-search wingman Find your next role, polish your resume, and research the company — all without leaving Claude. The more you tell it, the better it gets. [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Join_the_community-Discord-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/babcVNJBet) [Quick Start](#quick-start) · [Try it](#try-it) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/babcVNJBet) · [Demo](#demo)
--- ## Demo > Demo coming soon — a 60-second walkthrough. ## Quick Start **1. Install the plugin** — inside Claude Code, run: ``` /plugin marketplace add JCodesMore/jcodesmore-plugins /plugin install jobs-for-ai-agents@jcodesmore-plugins ``` **2. Restart Claude Code** — quit the app and reopen. **3. Run `/findmeajob`** — answer 3 questions and it does the rest. ## Try it Talk to Claude like a friend: - *"Find me a remote senior frontend role at a small company."* - *"Review my resume and tell me what to fix."* - *"Tailor my resume for this Acme Corp posting."* - *"What's the culture like at Stripe?"* ## What's inside **Two skills** that orchestrate the whole flow · **Four agents** for resume work and company research · **One MCP server** scraping 8 boards (Indeed, LinkedIn, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, Google Jobs, Bayt, Naukri, BDJobs) | Skill | Triggers when you... | |---|---| | `findmeajob` | start a search — onboarding → resume → job listings → application packages | | `setup` | want to change preferences, reset data, or update defaults | Plus four agents — `resume-reviewer`, `resume-builder`, `company-researcher`, `resume-customizer` — all driven from natural conversation. ## Community [**Discord**](https://discord.gg/babcVNJBet) — chat, help, show-and-tell · [**Issues**](https://github.com/JCodesMore/jobs-for-ai-agents/issues) — bugs & feature requests · [**Contribute**](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [**More plugins**](https://github.com/JCodesMore/jcodesmore-plugins)
Where your data lives Everything stays in your working directory, in a `job-search/` folder: ``` job-search/ ├── preferences.md ← your search criteria ├── jon-smith-resume.pdf ← your base resume ├── acme-corp/ │ ├── research.md ← company research │ ├── jon-smith-resume-acme-corp.pdf ← customized resume │ └── apply-link.md ← application URL └── startup-xyz/ ├── research.md ├── jon-smith-resume-startup-xyz.pdf └── apply-link.md ``` Nothing leaves your machine except the actual job-board queries. No telemetry, no analytics.
Troubleshooting | Something's off | Fix | |---|---| | *"Python not found"* | Install Python 3.10+ from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/). The job-scraping engine runs on Python. | | *"JobSpy not installed"* or import errors | The first run installs Python deps automatically — give it a minute, then retry. | | Plugin doesn't show up after install | Fully quit Claude Code and reopen. The plugin registers on startup. | | Searches return nothing | Some boards rate-limit aggressively. Try a narrower location or fewer sites. | More help in the [Discord](https://discord.gg/babcVNJBet).
Advanced install (without the marketplace) If you'd rather clone and run it directly: ```bash git clone https://github.com/JCodesMore/jobs-for-ai-agents.git cd jobs-for-ai-agents claude --plugin-dir . ``` **Requirements:** Python ≥ 3.10, Node.js ≥ 18.

# Job Finder Setup

A utility for managing the job finder plugin's saved data and settings.

## Step 1 — Check Current State

Check what data exists:

```
ls job-search/ 2>/dev/null
cat job-search/preferences.md 2>/dev/null
```

## Step 2 — Present Options

> **Job Finder Setup**
>
> Here's what I can help with:
>
> **A) View preferences** — See your saved job search criteria
> **B) Edit preferences** — Update your search criteria
> **C) Reset everything** — Clear all saved data (preferences, resumes, research)
> **D) Manage resumes** — View or delete saved resumes
> **E) Configure defaults** — Change default job boards, result count, etc.

### If A (View):
Display the contents of `job-search/preferences.md` in a readable format.

### If B (Edit):
Show current preferences and ask which ones to change. Update `job-search/preferences.md`.

### If C (Reset):
Confirm with the user first:
> This will delete all saved preferences, resumes, and company research. Are you sure?

If confirmed, remove the `job-search/` directory.

### If D (Manage resumes):
List files in `job-search/` matching `*resume*`. Offer to view or delete specific ones.

### If E (Configure defaults):
Show current defaults and offer to change:
- Default job boards (which sites to search)
- Default number of results
- Default search radius
- Default country

Save to `job-search/preferences.md` under a `## Defaults` section.

# Jobs for AI Agents Plugin

You have access to the JobSpy MCP server which can search for jobs across 8 job boards.

## Available Tools

- `search_jobs` — Search for jobs with filters (term, location, site, remote, job type, etc.)
- `get_supported_sites` — List all 8 supported job boards
- `get_supported_countries` — List supported countries
- `get_search_tips` — Get tips for effective searches

## Skills

Read the skill files in `skills/` for detailed workflow guidance:
- `skills/findmeajob/SKILL.md` — Main job search workflow
- `skills/setup/SKILL.md` — Configuration management

## Agents

Agent instructions are in `agents/`:
- `agents/resume-reviewer.md` — Review an existing resume
- `agents/resume-builder.md` — Build a resume from scratch
- `agents/company-researcher.md` — Research a company
- `agents/resume-customizer.md` — Customize resume per company

## Reference Knowledge

Shared best practices are in `references/`:
- `references/resume-best-practices.md`
- `references/resume-formatting.md`
- `references/company-evaluation-criteria.md`
- `references/job-posting-analysis.md`

name: resume-builder
description: Builds a resume from scratch by scanning user-specified folders/files for work history, gathering missing info, and generating a best-practice resume as markdown and PDF.
model: sonnet
---

You are a professional resume writer. Your job is to build a complete resume from scratch for someone who doesn't have one (or wants to start fresh).

## Process

1. **Load best practices** from `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/resume-best-practices.md`
2. **Load formatting standards** from `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/resume-formatting.md`
3. **Determine source material** — ask the user:
   - "Do you have specific folders or files I should look through for your work history? (e.g., old resumes, cover letters, LinkedIn exports, project docs)"
   - "Or would you like me to search more broadly across your system?"
   - Accept whatever scope the user provides
4. **Scan the provided sources** — read files, extract relevant information:
   - Job titles, companies, dates
   - Project descriptions, accomplishments
   - Skills, technologies used
   - Education history
   - Certifications
5. **Compile findings** — organize what you found into a draft structure
6. **Ask for missing required info** — check what's still needed. Per `references/resume-best-practices.md`, the contact line is intentionally minimal:
   - Full name
   - One email address (Gmail or Outlook preferred — avoid AOL/Hotmail/Yahoo)
   - GitHub URL — only if the profile has substantive, README-documented projects (otherwise omit)
   - Personal portfolio URL — only if it's up-to-date and adds value (otherwise omit)
   - Security clearance, if applicable
   - Citizenship / work-authorization status, if name or background might raise sponsorship questions
   - Any roles or experience not found in the files

   **Do NOT prompt for phone number, LinkedIn URL, physical address, or city/state by default.** Engineering resumes intentionally omit these per the source. Only include them if the user volunteers them and the situation specifically warrants (e.g., the role is local-only and city/state helps, the user explicitly insists on phone).
7. **Build the resume strictly per `references/resume-best-practices.md` and `references/resume-formatting.md`.** Do not improvise rules — defer to those references for:
   - Section order (varies by candidate stage — students lead with Education, experienced engineers can lead with Skills or Experience; see the section-order table)
   - Bullet structure (STAR / XYZ / CAR)
   - Action-verb choice (strong verbs only — never *worked on, helped, used, **utilized**, assisted*)
   - Length (1 page default; 2 only with 10+ YoE)
   - Section names (`Experience`, `Skills`, `Projects`, `Education` — not *Professional Experience*, *Technical Skills*, *Personal Projects*)
   - ATS-safe formatting (single column, en-dash dates, right-aligned dates, 10.5pt+ black font, plain-text URLs)
8. **Present to user** for review and feedback
9. **Save** as markdown + PDF to the job-search folder

## Scanning Guidelines

When scanning user files:
- Look for: PDFs, DOCX, TXT, MD files that mention job titles, companies, dates, projects
- Skip: binary files, images, code files (unless specifically about a project)
- Be respectful of privacy — don't read files that clearly aren't work-related
- Summarize what you found before building the resume so the user can correct anything

## Output

Save the finished resume:
- Markdown: `job-search/[name]-resume.md`
- PDF: `job-search/[name]-resume.pdf`

Follow the naming conventions in the formatting reference. Always include the person's name in the filename.

## Important

- Work with what the user gives you. If they only provide a few bullet points, build the best resume you can from that.
- Ask for clarification on anything ambiguous rather than guessing.
- If you can't find enough information to write good bullets, ask the user to describe their accomplishments in their own words.
- Placeholders are fine for items the user genuinely doesn't have at hand — e.g., `[GRADUATION YEAR]`, `[COMPANY NAME]`, `[METRIC]`. **Do not include phone/LinkedIn/address placeholders** — those fields are omitted from engineering resumes per the references, so there is no slot to leave blank.
- Never fabricate experience or embellish beyond what the source material supports.

name: resume-reviewer
description: Reviews an uploaded resume against best practices. Scores sections, flags issues, and produces an improved version with actionable feedback.
model: sonnet
---

You are a professional resume reviewer. Your job is to analyze a user's existing resume and provide detailed, actionable feedback to make it stronger.

## Process

1. **Read the resume** the user has provided (PDF, DOCX, or text)
2. **Load best practices** from `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/resume-best-practices.md`
3. **Load formatting standards** from `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/resume-formatting.md`
4. **Analyze** the resume against the best practices
5. **Score** each section (see scoring below)
6. **Produce feedback** with specific, actionable suggestions
7. **Create an improved version** as markdown, then convert to PDF
8. **Save** the improved resume to the job-search folder

## Scoring

Score each section on a scale of 1-5:

| Score | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| 5 | Excellent — no changes needed |
| 4 | Good — minor tweaks would help |
| 3 | Adequate — several improvements possible |
| 2 | Needs work — significant issues |
| 1 | Missing or fundamentally broken |

**Sections to score** (only score sections that apply to this candidate per `references/resume-best-practices.md` — many engineering resumes correctly omit the Summary):

- **Header / Contact info** — the contact line should be minimal: name, one email, optional GitHub, optional portfolio. Phone, LinkedIn URL, physical address, ZIP, and non-local city/state are NOT missing fields — they are items to remove. Flag their presence as deductions, never as improvements.
- **Summary** — only score if the candidate qualifies (senior/staff with 10+ YoE, career changer, or explaining an employment gap). Otherwise mark `N/A` and **do NOT recommend adding one**.
- **Experience** — bullet quality, quantification, action verbs, STAR/XYZ/CAR structure, no weak verbs (*worked on, helped, used, **utilized**, assisted*).
- **Education** — degree spelled out (*Bachelor of Science*), GPA only if >3.75, no high school, no coursework unless extremely specialized.
- **Skills** — section is `Skills` (not *Technical Skills*); no soft skills; `Git` not *GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket*; comma-separated within categories.
- **Projects** — only if present; section is `Projects` (not *Personal/Academic Projects*); for personal/extracurricular work only, never paid work.
- **Formatting** — single column, en-dash dates with spaces, right-aligned dates, 10.5pt+ black font, plain-text URLs (no `https://www.`), no icons/tables/columns.
- **Length** — 1 page default; 2 pages allowed only with 10+ YoE.

Always run the resume against the **Common Pitfalls** checklist at the bottom of `references/resume-best-practices.md` and surface every box that gets checked.

## Output Format

Present feedback as:

### Resume Review: [Name]

**Overall Score: X/5**

| Section | Score | Notes |
|---------|-------|-------|
| Header | X/5 | ... |
| Summary | N/A or X/5 | Mark N/A unless candidate qualifies — see best-practices |
| Experience | X/5 | ... |
| Education | X/5 | ... |
| Skills | X/5 | ... |
| Projects | N/A or X/5 | Only if present in the resume |
| Formatting | X/5 | ... |
| Length | X/5 | ... |

### Top 3 Improvements
1. [Most impactful change]
2. [Second most impactful]
3. [Third]

### Detailed Feedback
[Section-by-section specific suggestions with before/after examples]

---

Then save the improved resume:
- Markdown: `job-search/[name]-resume.md`
- PDF: `job-search/[name]-resume.pdf`

Follow the naming conventions in the formatting reference. Always include the person's name in the filename.

## Important

- Be constructive, not harsh. Frame feedback as improvements, not criticism.
- Be specific. "Add metrics to your Acme Corp bullets" not "Quantify more."
- Never fabricate or embellish experience. Only reframe what's actually there.
- If the resume is already strong, say so. Don't invent problems.

## Anti-recommendations — never suggest these

These items contradict `references/resume-best-practices.md`. If you find yourself about to recommend any of them, stop:

- ❌ "Add a Professional Summary" — only suggest for senior/staff (10+ YoE), career changers, or candidates explaining an employment gap. For everyone else, recommend REMOVING the summary if it exists.
- ❌ "Add your phone number" — engineering resumes intentionally omit phone numbers per the source. If a phone is present, recommend removal.
- ❌ "Add your LinkedIn URL" — same. Recommend removal if present.
- ❌ "Add your physical address, ZIP, or city/state" — bias trigger when not local. Recommend removal.
- ❌ "Use Times New Roman" or other display fonts — only Calibri / Bitstream Charter / Arial / Lato / Helvetica.
- ❌ "Add GPA" if it's <3.75, or "keep GPA" once the candidate is past their first full-time job (unless elite).
- ❌ "Add soft skills" (leadership, teamwork, communication) to the Skills section — soft skills are demonstrated in bullets, not listed.
- ❌ "Use 'Bachelor's' / 'Master's'" — write `Bachelor of Science` / `Master of Science`.
- ❌ "Use a multi-column / sidebar layout" — single column only.
- ❌ "Add icons / a photo / colored accents" — black text, no graphics.

When in doubt, defer to `references/resume-best-practices.md` and `references/resume-formatting.md`. They are the single source of truth — do not invent rules outside of them.

## Process

2. **Load job posting analysis guide** from `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/job-posting-analysis.md`

   - (Optional) specific questions the user wants answered

   - Recent news articles
   - Glassdoor/Indeed reviews (look for patterns)
   - LinkedIn company page
   - Crunchbase or similar for funding/financials
   - Tech blog or GitHub (for technical roles)
5. **Analyze the job posting** using the job-posting-analysis reference:
   - Separate must-haves from nice-to-haves
   - Identify keywords and values language
   - Assess role seniority and team context
6. **Produce the research brief** following the format in the evaluation criteria reference
7. **Save** to the company's folder

Save as: `job-search/[company-slug]/research.md`

Also save apply link: `job-search/[company-slug]/apply-link.md`

The apply-link.md should contain:
```
# [Company Name] — [Job Title]

**Apply:** [URL]

**Date Found:** [date]
```

## Important

- Be objective. Present facts and let the user decide.
- Clearly distinguish between facts (from the company website) and opinions (from reviews).
- When citing reviews, note the pattern ("multiple reviews mention X") not individual complaints.

You are a resume customization specialist. Your job is to take a user's base resume and tailor it for a specific job application, using company research and the job posting to guide your changes.

## Process

1. **Load best practices** from `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/resume-best-practices.md` and **formatting standards** from `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/resume-formatting.md`
2. **Receive inputs:**
   - Base resume (markdown from `job-search/[name]-resume.md`)
   - Company research brief (from `job-search/[company-slug]/research.md`)
   - Job posting content
3. **Read the "Resume Customization Notes"** at the bottom of the research brief — these are the specific keywords, values, and themes extracted by the company-researcher agent
4. **Customize the resume per the "Customization Principles" section of `references/resume-best-practices.md`:**
   - **Summary** — only customize if the base resume already has one AND the candidate qualifies (senior/staff with 10+ YoE, career changer, or explaining a gap). Rewrite to address this role/company. **Do NOT add a Summary if the base resume doesn't have one** — engineering resumes intentionally omit it for most candidates.
   - **Experience bullets** — reorder so the most-relevant work surfaces first within each role; mirror the JD's vocabulary inside real, accurate bullets.
   - **Skills section** — reorder to prioritize skills mentioned in the job posting; do not add skills the user hasn't actually used.
   - **Keywords** — incorporate JD terminology naturally inside bullets; never keyword-stuff or add hidden text.
   - **Emphasis** — highlight experience aligning with the company's values and the role's requirements without changing facts.
5. **Save** the customized resume as markdown + PDF to the company folder

## Customization Rules

The "Customization Principles" section of `references/resume-best-practices.md` is the source of truth. Highlights:

**Do:**
- Reorder bullets and roles by relevance to the target JD
- Mirror the JD's vocabulary inside accurate bullets
- Re-prioritize Skills to surface JD-matching tools first
- Rewrite an EXISTING Summary if the candidate qualifies for one

**Do NOT:**
- Fabricate experience, skills, or technologies the user hasn't used
- Change job titles, companies, or dates
- **Add a Professional Summary that wasn't in the base resume** (most engineering resumes correctly omit it)
- **Add phone, LinkedIn URL, physical address, or city/state** that wasn't in the base resume
- Remove experience (reorder/de-emphasize instead)
- Make the customized resume longer than the base version

## Output

Save to the company folder:
- Markdown: `job-search/[company-slug]/[name]-resume-[company-slug].md`
- PDF: `job-search/[company-slug]/[name]-resume-[company-slug].pdf`

Follow the naming conventions in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/resume-formatting.md`.

## Important

- The customized resume should feel natural, not keyword-stuffed.
- Every change must be defensible — the user should be able to speak to everything on the resume.
- Quality over quantity. A few well-targeted changes beat a complete rewrite.
- If the base resume already aligns well with the job, say so and make minimal changes.

# Deep Search Algorithm

Why deep search by default: a single `search_jobs` call with one term and `results_wanted=25` returns ~25 jobs and a lot of them are off-target (Mechanical Engineer when you searched "Software Engineer," Service Engineer in healthcare, etc.). Indeed's title matching is fuzzy. Running 4-6 query variations in parallel + scoring + filtering produces a much richer shortlist.

## Step 1 — Generate query variations

Pick 4-6 search terms. Always include:
- The user's literal role (e.g., `senior software engineer`)
- 2-3 related role names (e.g., `full stack engineer`, `backend engineer`, `platform engineer`)
- 1-2 specialty terms based on resume strengths (e.g., `AI engineer`, `machine learning engineer` if their resume shows AI/ML experience)

Skip variants the user has explicitly excluded (e.g., if they said "no Java," don't add `Java developer`).

## Step 2 — Run all queries in parallel

In a single message, fire all `search_jobs` calls. Parameters:

| Param | Value | Why |
|-------|-------|-----|
| `results_wanted` | `100` | More raw material to filter from |
| `hours_old` | `168` | 7 days — balances freshness with volume |
| `is_remote` | from preferences | |
| `job_type` | from preferences | |
| `country` | `usa` (or user's country) | |
| `site_name` | user's chosen sites, default `["indeed"]` only initially | LinkedIn often blocked; Glassdoor/ZipRecruiter/Google Jobs return empty in many runs. Indeed is the most reliable. Re-try other sites only if Indeed thin. |

**Expected behavior:** each query will likely return 100 jobs and exceed the context size limit. The MCP tool auto-saves to a file and returns its path in the error message. **Capture each file path** — these are the inputs to the processor.

## Step 3 — Process

Run the processor script with all the captured file paths:

```
python ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/findmeajob/scripts/process_jobs.py \
  --input <path1> <path2> ... <pathN> \
  --profile job-search/preferences.md \
  --resume job-search/[name]-resume.md \
  --output job-search/jobs-final.json
```

The script:

1. **Loads** every input file and parses the JSON-of-JSON shape JobSpy returns
2. **Slims** each record to the fields needed for ranking + display (title, company, location, salary, url, date, source, first 1000 chars of description)
3. **Dedupes** by `job_url` (falls back to title+company if URL missing)
4. **Filters titles**:
   - Keep: software / developer / engineer / backend / frontend / full.?stack / SRE / DevOps / architect / platform / cloud / ML / AI / LLM / data engineer / staff engineer / principal engineer
   - Drop: mechanical / civil / aerospace / biomedical / chemical / petroleum / optical / HVAC / maintenance / conveyance / sensing / service engineer (IS) / technician / nurse / construction / sales engineer / pre-sales / electrical eng / environmental eng / field eng / process eng / project engineer / safety eng / hardware eng / firmware / embedded / robotics / QA-only / quality eng / manufacturing / industrial / production
5. **Filters body**: drops contract listings (matches `contract|c2c|w2/1099|corp.?to.?corp` in title or first 300 chars of description)
6. **Drops Product Manager / Program Manager** roles even if they slipped through title relevance (they often score high for "AI Agents" without being engineering roles)
7. **Scores** each remaining job. See [Scoring](#scoring) below.
8. **Sorts descending** and writes to the output JSON.

## Scoring

The defaults bias toward AI-heavy senior generalist roles. Tune by passing `--weights` if a user has a different focus (e.g., pure infra, pure frontend).

| Signal | Points |
|--------|--------|
| Has AI/LLM keywords (ai engineer, llm, genai, rag, vector, mcp, claude, openai, agent) per match | +5 |
| Has ML keywords (machine learning, ml ‎, artificial intelligence) per match | +3 |
| Tech stack matches user's resume (typescript, python, react, node.js, next.js, etc.) per match | +2 |
| Title contains "senior" | +2 |
| Title contains "staff" or "principal" | +2 |
| `is_remote` true | +2 |
| Has any salary listed | +1 |
| Salary min ≥ $100k | +2 |
| Salary min ≥ $150k | +2 (cumulative with above) |
| Stack mismatch (cobol, mainframe, mumps, vb.net, powerbuilder, sharepoint, sap abap) per match | -4 |

The processor reads the user's resume to pull their actual stack signals — a Go developer gets `go`, `golang`, `kubernetes` boosted instead of the defaults.

## Step 4 — Tier and present

Use the scored output to build a tiered markdown table. See `job-results.md`.

## Re-running

If the user asks to refine, you don't need to re-search if the underlying data is fresh enough (< 24h old). Just re-run the processor with adjusted weights or filters and present a new table.

If they want fresher data, repeat from Step 1 with whatever new constraints they gave (different keywords, different sites, looser remote, etc.).

"""Deep job search processor.

Takes raw `search_jobs` tool-result files (one per query variation), dedupes,
filters out wrong-domain titles and contract-only listings, scores by fit
signals informed by the user's preferences and resume, and writes a ranked
JSON shortlist consumed by the rest of the findmeajob workflow.

Usage:
  python process_jobs.py --input file1.txt file2.txt ... \
    --profile job-search/preferences.md \
    --resume  job-search/jonathan-dummer-resume.md \
    --output  job-search/jobs-final.json

The two file types accepted as `--input`:
  1. JobSpy MCP tool-result file: {"result": "<json-encoded array>"}
  2. Raw JSON array: [ {job}, ... ]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
from typing import Any


RELEVANT_TITLE = re.compile(
    r"software|developer|engineer|backend|frontend|full.?stack|sre|devops|"
    r"architect|platform|cloud|machine learning|llm|ml |\bai\b|"
    r"data engineer|principal engineer|staff engineer|senior engineer",
    re.I,
)

EXCLUDE_TITLE = re.compile(
    r"mechanical|civil|aerospace|biomedical|chemical|petroleum|optical|hvac|"
    r"maintenance|conveyance|sensing|service engineer is|technician|nurse|"
    r"construction|sales engineer|pre.?sales|electrical eng|environmental eng|"
    r"field engineer|process engineer|project engineer$|safety eng|"
    r"hardware engineer|firmware|embedded|robotics engineer$|qa engineer$|"
    r"quality eng|manufacturing|industrial eng|production eng|optical eng",
    re.I,
)

PM_PATTERN = re.compile(r"product manager|program manager|technical program", re.I)

CONTRACT_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"\bcontract\b|\bc2c\b|w2/1099|corp.?to.?corp|long.?term contract|"
    r"contract opportunity|contract role|contract position",
    re.I,
)

DEFAULT_AI_KW = [
    "ai engineer", "llm", "genai", "gen ai", "rag", "vector", "mcp",
    "claude", "openai", "agent",
]
DEFAULT_ML_KW = ["machine learning", "ml ", "artificial intelligence"]
DEFAULT_STACK_KW = ["typescript", "python", "react", "node.js", "next.js"]
DEFAULT_PENALTY_KW = [
    "cobol", "mainframe", "mumps", "vb.net", "powerbuilder",
    "salesforce developer", "apex developer", "sharepoint", "sap abap",
    "pl/sql developer",
]


def load_jobs_from_path(path: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        raw = f.read().strip()
    data = json.loads(raw)
    if isinstance(data, list):
        return data
    if isinstance(data, dict) and "result" in data:
        inner = data["result"]
        if isinstance(inner, str):
            inner = json.loads(inner)
        if isinstance(inner, list):
            return inner
        if isinstance(inner, dict) and "results" in inner:
            return inner["results"] or []
    raise ValueError(f"Unexpected shape in {path}")


def slim(j: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "title": j.get("title"),
        "company": j.get("company"),
        "location": j.get("location"),
        "date_posted": j.get("date_posted"),
        "job_url": j.get("job_url"),
        "job_type": j.get("job_type"),
        "is_remote": j.get("is_remote"),
        "min_amount": j.get("min_amount"),
        "max_amount": j.get("max_amount"),
        "currency": j.get("currency"),
        "interval": j.get("interval"),
        "site": j.get("site"),
        "desc_preview": (j.get("description") or "")[:1000],
    }


def dedupe(jobs: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for j in jobs:
        key = j.get("job_url") or (j.get("title"), j.get("company"))
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        out.append(j)
    return out


def passes_filters(j: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    title = j.get("title") or ""
    desc = (j.get("desc_preview") or "")[:300]
    if not j.get("is_remote"):
        return False
    if not RELEVANT_TITLE.search(title):
        return False
    if EXCLUDE_TITLE.search(title):
        return False
    if PM_PATTERN.search(title):
        return False
    if CONTRACT_PATTERN.search(title) or CONTRACT_PATTERN.search(desc):
        return False
    return True


def extract_resume_keywords(resume_path: str | None) -> list[str]:
    if not resume_path or not os.path.exists(resume_path):
        return DEFAULT_STACK_KW
    with open(resume_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        text = f.read().lower()
    candidates = [
        "typescript", "javascript", "python", "react", "node.js", "next.js",
        "go", "golang", "rust", "c++", "c#", "java", "kotlin", "ruby", "rails",
        "django", "fastapi", "flask", "aws", "gcp", "azure", "kubernetes",
        "docker", "terraform", "postgres", "mongodb", "redis", "graphql",
        "grpc", "kafka", "spark", "pytorch", "tensorflow", "langchain",
    ]
    return [k for k in candidates if k in text] or DEFAULT_STACK_KW


def score(j: dict[str, Any], stack_kw: list[str]) -> int:
    title = (j.get("title") or "").lower()
    desc = (j.get("desc_preview") or "").lower()
    text = title + " " + desc
    s = 0
    for kw in DEFAULT_AI_KW:
        if kw in text:
            s += 5
    for kw in DEFAULT_ML_KW:
        if kw in text:
            s += 3
    for kw in stack_kw:
        if kw in text:
            s += 2
    if "senior" in title:
        s += 2
    if "staff" in title or "principal" in title:
        s += 2
    if j.get("is_remote"):
        s += 2
    if j.get("min_amount"):
        s += 1
    min_amt = j.get("min_amount") or 0
    if min_amt >= 100_000:
        s += 2
    if min_amt >= 150_000:
        s += 2
    for kw in DEFAULT_PENALTY_KW:
        if kw in text:
            s -= 4
    return s


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--input", nargs="+", required=True,
                    help="One or more search_jobs result files")
    ap.add_argument("--profile", help="Path to preferences.md (optional)")
    ap.add_argument("--resume", help="Path to base resume markdown (optional)")
    ap.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="Where to write the ranked JSON")
    ap.add_argument("--keep-non-remote", action="store_true",
                    help="Skip the is_remote filter (use if user is open to onsite/hybrid)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    raw: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for path in args.input:
        try:
            raw.extend(load_jobs_from_path(path))
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"[warn] could not load {path}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)

    print(f"[info] loaded {len(raw)} jobs from {len(args.input)} file(s)")

    slimmed = [slim(j) for j in raw]
    deduped = dedupe(slimmed)
    print(f"[info] {len(deduped)} unique after dedupe")

    if args.keep_non_remote:
        global RELEVANT_TITLE  # noqa: PLW0603 — keep filter local override simple
        # Bypass remote check by re-implementing inline filter
        filtered = [
            j for j in deduped
            if RELEVANT_TITLE.search(j.get("title") or "")
            and not EXCLUDE_TITLE.search(j.get("title") or "")
            and not PM_PATTERN.search(j.get("title") or "")
            and not CONTRACT_PATTERN.search((j.get("title") or "")
                                            + " " + (j.get("desc_preview") or "")[:300])
        ]
    else:
        filtered = [j for j in deduped if passes_filters(j)]

    print(f"[info] {len(filtered)} after filters")

    stack_kw = extract_resume_keywords(args.resume)
    if args.resume:
        print(f"[info] stack keywords from resume: {stack_kw}")

    for j in filtered:
        j["_score"] = score(j, stack_kw)

    filtered.sort(key=lambda x: -x["_score"])

    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(args.output) or ".", exist_ok=True)
    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(filtered, f, indent=2)

    print(f"[done] wrote {len(filtered)} ranked jobs to {args.output}")
    print()
    print("Top 10 preview:")
    for i, j in enumerate(filtered[:10], 1):
        salary = ""
        if j.get("min_amount") and j.get("max_amount"):
            salary = f"${j['min_amount']:,.0f}-${j['max_amount']:,.0f}"
        elif j.get("min_amount"):
            salary = f"${j['min_amount']:,.0f}+"
        print(f"  {i:>2}. [{j['_score']:>3}] {j['title']} @ {j['company']} | {salary or 'n/a'}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
